defects.title: A reporter abbreviation was parsed as an appendix record citation
defects.severity: evidence attached to the wrong source
defects.observed_before: extract_record_cites reported two appendix citations: 'App. 306, 571' at span (4098,4111) with pin '306', and 'App. 2004' at span (9280,9289). Both are the reporter abbreviation 'Colo. App.'; the first took the parallel reporter's volume (571) as the appendix page.

root_cause.detail: The appendix pattern matched the 'App.' inside 'Colo. App.' with no guard for a preceding reporter token. The false cites also entered caselaw/authorities.py::_keep_supported_id_forms as intervening citations, which can suppress a legitimate Id. attachment.

repair.detail: Reject an appendix match whose immediately preceding abbreviation token is a reporter tail (Colo., C. in N.C., Ill., Ind., Fla., Ct., ...), unless the text before 'App.' names a document (Appellant's, Joint, Record, App. to).

defects.verified_after: record cites on the fixture: 2 -> 0. 'App. 58', 'Appellant's App. 136-38' still extracted.

defects.title: OCR discarded the whole page table, so no citation had a page
defects.severity: lost page provenance and viewer highlights
defects.observed_before: POST /api/documents to the live service answered textSource=ocr pageCount=2 with pages=[] and highlights=[]. Every citation span in a scanned filing had no page.

root_cause.detail: upload_document set pages = [] when OCR text replaced the embedded text, because the embedded-layer offsets no longer described the text. The information needed to rebuild them existed but was discarded: OcrResult.page_chars counts stripped text, so it cannot rebuild offsets, and the raw per-page length was never recorded.

repair.detail: Record the verbatim length of each recognised page, and rebuild the response page table from it. Only pages carrying text get a range, so no offset resolves to two pages and the table covers the whole text.

defects.verified_after: in-process repaired checkout on the real scan: pageCount 2, pages_table 2, highlights 1 (all with a page), page_table_last_end 1386 == text_length 1386, spans_ambiguous 0, spans_without_page 0.
defects.remaining: Not live. The port 8010 process still answers pages_table 0 for the same file until Codex restarts it.

defects.title: Blank pages inside a text-layer filing were never disclosed
defects.observed_before: warning was null. The document-wide average is 1,400 characters per page, far above _MIN_CHARS_PER_PAGE, so neither branch of _text_layer_warning fired.

root_cause.detail: Only a document-wide average was tested, so a partial scan inside a normal filing was invisible. The checklist names this failure by name (B05): no silent empty extraction or page loss.

repair.detail: Also report pages that carry almost no text, naming the page numbers and summarising when there are many.

defects.verified_after: the real 50-page filing now reports: '3 of 50 page(s) carry almost no text (pages 1, 31, 40). Those pages may be scans, photographs or images, and any citation printed on them is missing from this result.'

defects.title: Hallucinated OCR could replace a real but thin text layer

input.path: synthetic two-page PDF with one short citation per page

defects.observed_before: The upload path replaced the embedded text with Tesseract output whenever the OCR text was longer. On a page whose embedded layer held one exact case citation, Tesseract returned more characters than the layer did, so garbled recognition replaced text already present in the document.

root_cause.detail: The gate to try OCR was _text_layer_warning (which fires below 100 characters per page) and the gate to accept it was 'longer', so a thin-but-exact layer could be overwritten by recognition noise.

repair.detail: Try OCR only below 20 characters per page, where the layer is unusable rather than merely thin. Between 20 and 100 characters per page the layer is kept and disclosed through EXT-3's warning.

defects.regression: covered by tests/test_document_pages.py (the embedded-layer upload test would otherwise become OCR)
defects.verified_after: a two-page PDF with a short embedded citation keeps textSource=embedded and its exact text.

defects.title: A repeated full citation lost the short name printed in front of it
defects.severity: naming evidence dropped; false parties_unverified flag
defects.observed_before: Both occurrences returned plaintiff=None, defendant=None, case_name=None and the flag "parties_unverified: eyecite reported '' v. 'Rule 12(b)(5). Warne'". The filing prints the name on the page.

root_cause.detail: Two parts. (1) The short name was read from metadata.antecedent_guess, which is always None on the pinned eyecite version, so the branch never fired. (2) The available substitute, metadata.defendant, crosses sentence boundaries and reported 'Rule 12(b)(5). Warne' for one occurrence, so adopting it directly would name a case after a rule citation.

repair.detail: Derive the name from the last clause before the citation with an abbreviation-aware sentence boundary, validate it as capitalized tokens with known connectors, and refuse a lone introductory signal. Non-adversarial clauses are delegated to the existing _derive_case_name.

defects.verified_after: both occurrences carry case_name='Warne'; parties_unverified flags in the fixture 2 -> 1 (the remaining one is a parallel reporter with no name in its own window, which is correct); groups without a caseName 0; groups 10.

defects.title: Typographic ligatures and accents dropped the whole party caption
defects.severity: naming evidence lost; downstream caption mismatch
defects.observed_before: _derive_parties returned (None, None) for a full caption; the citation group was the only unnamed group in the 21-document corpus outside its index.

root_cause.detail: Party character classes accepted only ASCII letters and the head was a literal [A-Z], so a ligature ended the match early and no party was captured.

repair.detail: Accept any Unicode letter in a party and move the 'must open on a capital' rule into a lookahead so lower-case prose is still rejected.

defects.verified_after: the unnamed-group count on the 21-document corpus went 39 -> 38; the remaining 38 are all in 00-INDEX.pdf, whose table of authorities prints names and citations in separate columns.

defects.title: Subsequent history became a separate group named after the wrong case
defects.severity: evidence attached to the wrong authority
defects.observed_before: A filing writing '..., aff'd, 908 F.3d 1219' produced two groups. The history group had no party and no name, and the only caption before it belonged to the case it affirms.

root_cause.detail: The merge recognised a parallel reporter gap (a pin and a comma) but had no rule for a history phrase, so the affirmance never joined its case.

repair.detail: Accept a gap made of a pin, the original's own court-and-year parenthetical, and a history phrase. Commas inside a parenthetical are not separators. A history merge keeps the later citation's own year, court and pin, because an affirmance is a different decision of the same case.

defects.verified_after: on the three real filings the rule accepts exactly 2 merges, both correct in context, and refuses 0 that should have merged. Unnamed groups in that three-document sample went 8 -> 6. On the 21-document corpus the rule accepts 0 (no filing there carries subsequent history), so it changes nothing there.

open_gaps.title: Seven real-filing citation groups carry no naming evidence at all
open_gaps.evidence: scripts/audit_naming_coverage.py over the 21 orderbench PDFs plus five real storage filings: 400 groups, 330 named from parties, 25 named from a caption on a non-header member, 45 with no naming evidence on any member. All 20 orderbench briefs are 100 percent named; every one of the 45 sits in an index or in one of five real filings.
open_gaps.impact: A group with no name cannot be checked for identity downstream, so the identity stage has nothing to compare. The filing in every sampled case does print the name.
distinct_causes: A markdown index table prints the name and the citation in separate cells (all 38 in 00-INDEX.pdf).

A real table of authorities prints the case name on one line and the citation on the next, separated by a dot leader (1e2056140eda449b9faaf2db9c5652a2.pdf g12, 'Fantasy, Inc. v. Fogerty' / '510 U.S. 517').
A citation inside a nested parenthetical takes the inner caption (0385b985cbe443ba9e7e297f664764c3.pdf g8).
A caption shaped 'Case, No. CIV 16-0318 JB/SCY,' is not read (23fb36fee64f48aa952c765bfc3be0e7.pdf g2).
A name that wraps onto the line before its citation is missed (359a46773baa472d832558e027afa22e.pdf g6, 'Trinidad Sch. Dist. No. 1 v.' / 'Lopez, 963 P.2d 1095').
open_gaps.next_step: Pair a table row's name with its citation before grouping, and teach the caption matcher the wrapped and docket-bearing shapes. Read-only database work is not involved.
